instruction.text: Daniel is going to the dentist. He wants to find out more about his teeth, so he asks the dentist some questions. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Why are all my teeth different shapes?
atoms.sound: Why are all my teeth different shapes?

atoms.b: That’s a good question. Each of our teeth have ((++different the_same)) jobs to do so that our food can be ((++swallowed spat_out)) and passed on to the ((++digestive circulatory)) system.
What do these flat teeth at the front do?
The flat teeth are called ((++incisors canines)), their job is to ((++cut grind)) up the food. Imagine biting into an apple: your incisors are what cut through the fruit.
And what about the pointy ones next to the incisors?
Those are called ((++canines molars)). The role of these teeth is to rip and ((++tear crush)) the food into smaller pieces. Their ((++pointy round)) shape helps them to do this more effectively.
What are the teeth at the back for?
The back teeth are known as ((++molars enamel)). They do most of the ((++chewing swallowing)) and prepare the food to be swallowed by ((++grinding building)) it up.
Wow! I had no idea they were all so different.

instruction.text: Decide if the facts are about milk teeth or permanent teeth.

hint.text:
Milk teeth are also known as baby teeth. They are the 20 teeth we have during our childhood that begin to fall out when we are around 5 years old.

Then our permanent teeth grow in. These 32 teeth must last for the rest of our lives.
hint.label: Teeth

atoms.b: These teeth start to fall out when we are around 5 years old.
These teeth grow in once we are around 6 months old.
They are the teeth we use most in our lifetimes.

instruction.text: Once our milk teeth fall out, our teeth have to last our entire lifetime. How can we look after our teeth? Select all the correct options.

b: ++Not having too many sugary foods or drinks

feedback.end: It is also good to use toothpaste with fluoride in it. Some scientists think this helps keep our teeth strong.
